q: State the sex of P and of S.
P is female; S is male (a Y chromosome is present).
Identify the conditions shown by Q, R and S.
Q: Down syndrome (trisomy 21). R: Turner syndrome. S: Klinefelter syndrome.
Explain how R could arise.
Non-disjunction of the sex chromosomes in meiosis in one parent gave a gamete with no sex chromosome; it was fertilised by a gamete carrying an X.
Explain why S is male, even though S has two X chromosomes.
Sex is decided by the Y chromosome: its SRY gene triggers testis development, however many X chromosomes there are.
Suggest what the match between human chromosome 2 and two chimpanzee chromosomes shows.
Two ancestral chromosomes fused in the human line after it split from chimpanzees: evidence of common ancestry.
Calculate how many times larger the human genome is than the fruit fly’s, and compare with the change in gene number.
3100 / 140 = 22 times larger, but only 20 000 / 13 900 = 1.4 times as many genes.
Calculate the number of genes per million bp in E. coli and in humans.
E. coli 4300 / 4.6 = about 930. Human 20 000 / 3100 = about 6.5.
Explain why genome size is a poor guide to how complex an organism is.
Large genomes are mostly non-coding DNA (repeats, transposons): the lily’s genome is about 48 times larger than ours.
Bread wheat has about five times as many genes as humans. Suggest why.
Wheat is polyploid (hexaploid): it combines the genomes of three ancestral species, so it has several copies of most genes.
Suggest why a small genome is an advantage to bacteria.
It can be copied quickly with fewer nucleotides and less energy, so the cells can divide fast.
